chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Sama'a, from one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the crops — what is subject to zakat from them? He said: Wheat, barley, corn, rice, rye, and lentils — all of these are among what zakat must be paid on.
And he said: Everything measured by the sa'a that reaches the awsaq threshold — zakat is due upon it.

key_terms.الأوساق: Plural of wasq — a unit of dry measure; five awsaq is the nisab threshold for zakat on grains (approximately 650 kg)
key_terms.الزكاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.السلت: A variety of barley without a husk, sometimes translated as rye or naked barley
key_terms.الصاع: A traditional volumetric measure used in Islamic jurisprudence (approximately 3 kg of wheat)

ai.seo_question: Which grains require zakat in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked which agricultural products are subject to zakat. He named six specific grains — wheat, barley, corn, rice, rye, and lentils — and then gave a general rule: any grain measured by the sa'a that meets the minimum threshold (awsaq) is subject to zakat. This ruling situates the obligation of agricultural zakat within a precise jurisprudential framework, defining both the qualifying commodities and the minimum quantity that triggers the obligation.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from ahmad Bin Sama’at, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the farm, what would be purified (Zakāt paid) from it?’
So heasws said: ‘The wheat, and the barley, and the corn, and the rice, and the rye, and the lentils – all of these are from what would be purified (Zakāt paid)’.
And heasws said: ‘Everything which is weighed by the Sa’a, so it reaches the Awsaaq, so upon it is the Zakāt’.
